Answers.content:
The task to calculate the number of ways to travel from O to P using 1 bus seems unnecessary given the problem statement because there are no other places between N and Q. The journey from M to Q involves traveling through the sequence M → N → O → P → Q, but since there is only one way to travel from O to P (using 1 bus), this task does not add any value to the overall calculation of the total number of ways to travel from M to Q.

The total number of ways to travel from M to Q can be calculated by multiplying the number of ways to travel between each consecutive pair of places:

- From M to N: 3 buses
- From N to O: 4 buses
- From O to P: 1 bus (as there is only one way)
- From P to Q: 3 buses

Thus, the total number of ways is \(3 \times 4 \times 1 \times 3 = 36\).

Therefore, the task "BusJourneyOP" can be considered redundant in this context.

Thus, the total number of ways to travel from O to Q via P is \(1 \times 3 = 3\).
